svg.title: The Twelve-Factor App
svg.desc: The Twelve-Factor App. Twelve rules for apps that deploy cleanly anywhere: config in the environment, stateless processes, separate build, release and run. Step 1, A pet server: catalog-01: password in Git, sessions in memory, logs on disk; a second server logs shoppers out. Step 2, Code and config (I–V): One repo builds catalog:2.3.0 once; each environment's config makes it v41-staging or v41-prod. Step 3, Running it (VI–IX): Sessions move to Redis, web scales to 6 pods and worker to 2; pods start in 2 s, drain on SIGTERM. Step 4, Operating it, and limits: PostgreSQL 16 in dev, logs on stdout, the migration as a Job; limits: secrets, databases, telemetry.

g.text: catalog-01: password in Git, sessions in memory, logs on disk; a second server logs shoppers out.
One repo builds catalog:2.3.0 once; each environment's config makes it v41-staging or v41-prod.
Sessions move to Redis, web scales to 6 pods and worker to 2; pods start in 2 s, drain on SIGTERM.
PostgreSQL 16 in dev, logs on stdout, the migration as a Job; limits: secrets, databases, telemetry.
before: one hand-built server, changed by hand over SSH
build → release → run: three separate stages, and a release never changes
the platform adds, moves and replaces pods whenever it needs to
operating it: the same stack everywhere, logs as a stream, one-off tasks
written in 2011 for Heroku-style web apps: some parts need adapting
run: pods start from release v41-prod
nothing is changed on a running pod:
a fix or a setting means a new release
a new pod is ready 2 s after it starts
Kubernetes waits up to 30 s by default
the migration: a Job, not SSH
same image and config as v41-prod
its output joins the log stream
no log pipeline: app.log stays on catalog-01’s disk, and cron rotates the old files away
to read it: ssh catalog-01, then grep
each pod writes to stdout; the platform ships it
no telemetry or security factor: the 2024 revision is still open
